subject: Decision: DirectConnect (private link) vs PrivateLink vs IPsec for MerchantCo pilot
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@merchantco.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot kickoff — connectivity options (latency-sensitive checkout flows)

Hi Aditya / Connor —

Thanks again for the quick call this morning. As discussed, MerchantCo is running a small checkout-A/B pilot and needs predictable sub-50ms response for fraud-scoring calls from our US-west region. Security requires customer-managed private connectivity; our infra team asked for a short recommendation on tradeoffs between: (A) AWS DirectConnect/DirectConnect Hosted (we'll refer to it as DirectConnect) with a dedicated peer, (B) AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints to the Redwood VPC endpoint), and (C) site-to-site IPsec (managed by us using our firewall vendor).

Key constraints:
- Throughput during peak: ~200 RPS (burst to 500 for short windows)
- Source IP visibility required for downstream services
- No public internet exposure for requests or keys
- SOC2 evidence and firewall rules must be provisioned before pilot start (target: Nov 1)

Could you share your recommendation and an ops-runbook of the fallbacks? I've attached our initial mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Elena
MerchantCo — Infra

Attachments: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32KB)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@merchantco.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff — connectivity options (latency-sensitive checkout flows)

Elena —

Thanks for the clear brief and the MAP. Quick summary up-front: for MerchantCo's latency and security constraints I recommend DirectConnect when low and consistent latency is the priority and you can accept dedicated circuit provisioning lead time; PrivateLink is a good middle-ground for fast setup with strong isolation but source IP preservation is trickier; IPsec (S2S) is the lowest-gate friction but has the least predictable latency unless coupled with a managed SD-WAN.

Short bullets:
- DirectConnect (pros): consistent L3 path, easiest end-to-end latency budgeting, supports source IP preservation if you NAT/route appropriately. (cons): procurement/ordering (1–3 weeks), port costs, potential single-AZ vendor tie-in.
- PrivateLink (pros): quick to stand up from Redwood side, interface endpoints isolate service plane, no public IPs on the path. (cons): source IP shows the ENI by default unless we do proxying; egress costs can be higher; cross-account endpoint policies need careful config.
- IPsec S2S (pros): fastest proof-of-concept, uses your edge appliance, easier to iterate. (cons): latency variability, NAT complexity, operational burden on MerchantCo to maintain tunnels and BGP if desired.

Operational fallback proposal:
1) Start pilot with PrivateLink + per-request token authentication to get days-to-prod.
2) If latency tail or source IP requirements fail, move to DirectConnect with a short runway — we pre-share the circuit requirements (LOA) and test with a dedicated test VLAN.
3) Keep an IPsec backup for quick failover and for regions where DirectConnect isn't available.

I'll attach a short runbook and a sample network diagram in my next email. Connor will outline the traffic flows and firewall rules we expect you to mirror.

Best,
Aditya
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary, 18KB)

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@merchantco.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff — connectivity options (latency-sensitive checkout flows)

Elena —

Adding the operational perspective and an initial checklist. I've sketched a minimal network diagram (attached) showing three variants: DirectConnect private VIF → Redwood transit, PrivateLink endpoint → Redwood service ENI, and S2S (IPsec) to our edge gateway. Key notes:

DirectConnect runbook highlights:
- Provision private VIF to the region (we provide LOA + required prefixes).
- Configure BGP with MD5; we recommend /30 peerings and route-filter lists to restrict advertised prefixes.
- Health checks: BGP session monitoring + active HTTP latency probes to the pilot model endpoint.
- Failover: if DX uplink fails, traffic should fail over to the IPsec tunnel (we can implement route priority).

PrivateLink runbook highlights:
- MerchantCo creates an interface endpoint in your VPC and attaches an ENI. From Redwood side we accept endpoint connections with a scoped security group.
- To preserve caller identity, we propose a short-lived x-forwarded-for header that our edge adds after authenticating the TLS client credential — this preserves source insights for downstream systems without exposing raw LB IPs.
- Verify that endpoint policies allow only the MerchantCo account and restrict to specific subnets.

IPsec runbook highlights:
- Use IPsec with IKEv2 + strong ciphers; prefer routed mode with a /29 for the tunnel endpoints to enable source-IP pass-through testing.
- If you advertise internal prefixes over BGP, add route filters to prevent accidental propagation to other tenants.

I'll attach the diagram (merchant-network-diagram.png) and a short firewall ACL template.

Connor
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: merchant-network-diagram.png (PNG, 72KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@merchantco.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Oct 2028 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff — connectivity options (latency-sensitive checkout flows)

Elena — quick security callouts to help your compliance team sign off fast:

- SOC2 evidence: we'll provide the redwood-soc2-summary.pdf and our pen-test report on the endpoint plane; please add the attachment to your vendor intake.
- Endpoint authentication: prefer mTLS on top of the private transport. For PrivateLink we can accept a client cert at the connection and still add the x-forwarded-for header described by Connor.
- Key management: we do not retain customer keys in plaintext; if you require HSM-backed KMS integration on your side, we can outline the key-wrapping flow.
- Audit logging: all requests over the private link will be surfaced to the Console traces with token-level attribution; we can add an S3 delivery of raw logs to your account for retention.

If MerchantCo's compliance team wants the fastest green-light: 1) get a PrivateLink in place with mTLS and the MAP filled; 2) we run a short latency soak and share traces; 3) if you still miss SLOs, we switch the lane to DirectConnect while preserving the PrivateLink as a control-plane path.

Kimberly
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@merchantco.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2028 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff — connectivity options (latency-sensitive checkout flows)

Thanks all — this is great and actionable. Summary from our side:
- We'll stand up PrivateLink + mTLS first week (Ops will provision interface endpoint on Mon).
- We'll run a 72-hour latency soak with synthetic traffic and share traces with Redwood.
- If 95th/99th tail >50ms consistently, we will open a DirectConnect request (PO already approved) and aim to cutover in two weeks.
- We'll keep an IPsec tunnel as a hot-standby configured to auto-prefer in route tables if BGP fails.

Please send the endpoint policies and the firewall ACL template you referenced so our network team can pre-stage rules.

Elena
MerchantCo — Infra
